issues.where: the lower half of the globe, in front of the cottage and pond
issues.what: The swirl collapses into bright, continuous curved bands. At normal size it reads as a milky sheet pasted over the miniature rather than particles moving through liquid.
issues.fix: Break up the longest streaks, leave clear gaps between clusters, and use separate near and far particle layers so the pond and cottage intermittently show through.

issues.where: the glass-to-base junction in crops 9 and 12
issues.what: The thin blue edge of the sphere cuts straight into a bright, uninterrupted collar. There is no visible recess or narrow contact shadow to show how the glass is seated.
issues.fix: Recess the glass into the collar, expose a thin bevel at the seat, and add a tight contact shadow that follows the join.

issues.where: the suspended seeds and pinlights in crop 2
issues.what: Many of the larger tufts repeat the same face-on radial silhouette, while the green lights repeat the same round core and halo. Different sizes and blur levels help, but the repetition still reads as layered sprites.
issues.fix: Give the tufts different strand counts and side-on profiles, and vary the light cores and halos independently with depth.

issues.where: the ivy around the cottage doorway in crop 6
issues.what: The larger leaves and petals are flat, hard-edged polygons with single-tone faces. They look cut from colored card against the more convincing stonework.
issues.fix: Give the prominent leaves cupped profiles, irregular edges and subtle veins, and add small shadows where they overlap the masonry.

issues.where: the roof and its eaves in crop 3
issues.what: The shingle courses remain bare even with the feathery particles concentrated immediately above them. Nothing recognizable as the same material has caught on the roof.
issues.fix: Trap a few identifiable tufts against the eaves, chimney and shingle seams, with small contact shadows to distinguish them from airborne particles.

issues.where: the teal and blue inlays on the base in crops 8 and 10
issues.what: The inlays have nearly uniform domed shading and broad milky highlights. Next to the ridged shells and granular base, they read as molded plastic rather than worn glass.
issues.fix: Vary their surface roughness and edge thickness, and use subtle transmission and mottled frosting so thinner edges respond differently from their centers.
